title: Widget sync: how settings reach every device
summary: Widget sync carries settings from the hub to every enrolled device. This lesson covers the four stages of a run, who may change what, the three sync modes and when to use each, how retries work, and how to read a sync.yaml file.

points.text: A sync run collects, validates, packages and delivers settings, in that order.
points.quote: Each sync run moves through four stages: collect, validate, package and deliver.

points.text: A run that fails validation delivers nothing, so devices keep their last good settings.

example.title: Bringing back a device marked unreachable
example.situation: After a weekend power cut, one device at a site shows as unreachable on the Sync health page.
steps: Open the Sync health page and find the device's last status record.
Read why delivery stopped: after 8 failed retries the hub stopped trying.
Bring the device back online so that it checks in with the hub.
Confirm that the next sync run for the device is marked healthy.

slides.title: Every sync run has four stages
bullets: A failed validation stops the run
Devices keep their last good settings

narration.text: So what actually happens when the hub syncs a device?
Every run moves through four stages: it collects the settings, validates them, packages them and delivers them.
The order matters. Validation comes before anything leaves the hub.
So when validation fails, the run stops there, and devices simply keep their last good settings.

slides.title: Who can change sync
bullets: Site operators: their own sites only
Device owners: pause one device for up to 24 hours

narration.text: Can anyone with access change how sync works?
No. Hub administrators can change sync settings for the whole hub.
Site operators can change them for their own sites only, and a device owner can pause sync on one device for up to 24 hours.
And if the hub and a site disagree?
The most specific setting wins: a site setting beats the hub, and a device setting beats the site.

slides.title: Three ways to sync
bullets: Push: delivered as soon as it is published
Pull: each device asks on its own schedule
Mirror: devices read from a relay at the site

narration.text: There are three sync modes. Push mode delivers settings as soon as a hub administrator publishes them.
Pull mode lets each device ask the hub for changes on its own schedule.
Mirror mode keeps a full copy of the hub settings on a local relay at the site, and devices read from the relay.
What if the connection to the hub drops?
Push needs a live connection. Pull and mirror keep working, and mirror serves the last copy the relay received.

slides.title: Pick the mode for a site
bullets: Reliable link, changes at once: push

narration.text: How do I choose between them for a site?
Look at two things: how reliable the site's connection is, and how fast changes must arrive.
A reliable connection and changes that must arrive at once point to push mode.
If devices can wait for their next check, pull mode is enough. And for a site whose connection often drops, use mirror mode.
In pull mode each device checks the hub every 15 minutes by default.
You can set the interval anywhere from 5 to 240 minutes.
So shorter is better?
Not always. A shorter interval brings changes sooner, but it also sends more requests to the hub.

slides.title: When delivery fails
bullets: The first retry comes after 1 minute
Each wait doubles, up to 60 minutes

narration.text: What does the hub do when a device does not answer?
It waits and tries again. The first retry comes after one minute.
Each later retry waits twice as long as the one before, up to sixty minutes.
After eight failed retries the device is marked as unreachable, and the hub stops trying until the device checks in again.

slides.title: Inside the sync agent
bullets: Reporter: sends the result to the hub

narration.text: On every device, the sync agent does the work in four parts.
The scheduler starts each check, and the downloader fetches the settings package.
The verifier checks the package signature, and the reporter sends the result back to the hub.
And a package with a bad signature?
It is never applied.

slides.title: Reading a sync.yaml file
bullets: mode and interval_minutes: how a device checks
quiet_window: no new checks at night

narration.text: Here is a sync.yaml file. It sets pull mode with a thirty-minute interval.
The quiet window runs from ten at night to six in the morning. During it, the agent starts no new checks.
And a check that is already running?
It finishes. The retry block allows up to eight attempts, and results are reported to the hub.

slides.title: Rolling out a big change
bullets: Check Sync health before each stage

narration.text: For a large change, Contoso recommends a staged rollout.
Start with one pilot site on day one, extend to one region on day three, and to every site on day seven.
And between the stages?
Review the Sync health page before each stage, so a problem stays small.
